The studied Ni-Co-based superalloy has the following chemical compositions:25.0 Co, 14.0 Cr, 2.8 Mo, 1.2 W, 8.0 (Al, Ti, Nb), 0.02 C, 0.02 B, 0.03 Zr, and balanced Ni (wt%)
The alloy was prepared by vacuum induction melting and forging.
The alloy was prepared by vacuum induction melting and forging.
The samples were cut by electric spark cutting and homogenized at 1100 ◦C to eliminate the segregation.
Aging treatments were carried out as follows: 650◦C/24 h/air cooling + 760◦C/16 h/air cooling.
Aging treatments were carried out as follows: 650◦C/24 h/air cooling + 760◦C/16 h/air cooling.
The γ′ precipitates are L12 structures confirmed by the SAED patterns (Figure 3b,d,f) and are coherent with the γ matrix.
These three elements mainly form (Ni,Co) 3(Al,Ti) during the heat treatment process
Co, Cr, Mo, and W are enriched in the γ matrix and play the role of solid solution strengthening
the primary γ′ precipitates tend to appear at grain boundaries with larger sizes
the secondary γ′ precipitates are located within moderately sized grains
a large number of nanoscale tertiary γ′ precipitations can be seen inside the grains

attributes.morphology: mostly moving alone, some in pairs

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: Apparently, there are some dislocations in both the γ matrix and the γ′ precipitation at room temperature. Most of the dislocations move alone, some in pairs.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: When a partial dislocation is cut into the γ′ precipitation, high-energy APBs are generated due to the a/2<110> displacement of the superlattice.

attributes.morphology: two different directions, intersecting, similar to Lomer-Cottrell locks

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: When the testing temperature is 650 ◦C, the dislocation density becomes high and a number of SFs are produced both inside the γ′ precipitates and the γ matrix.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: The SFs were observed in two different directions, which formed structures similar to Lomer–Cottrell locks.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: the formation of dislocation entanglement in the γ matrix indicates that the deformation occurs mainly in the γ matrix

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: When the test temperature is 760 ◦C, it can be seen that the dislocation density in the γ matrix further increases, and they become entangled with each other.

attributes.size: twinned lamella thickness of 16 layers of atoms

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: when the test temperature is increased, a large number of deformation twins are generated in the alloy

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: The thickness of the twinned lamella is 16 layers of atoms.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: When the test temperature was 850 ◦C, it can be seen that more dislocations were formed in the γ matrix and tangled with each other (Figure 7a,b)

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: the stacking faults parallel to each other are clearly visible after the tensile test at 850 ◦C

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: A large number of dislocations surrounded the γ′ precipitates, while only a few dislocations were located in the γ′ precipitates.
The yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of the superalloy had similar variation trends with the temperature. The YS and UTS decreased slightly when the temperature rose to 650◦C
The yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of the superalloy had similar variation trends with the temperature.
The elongation decreased rapidly with temperature, from room temperature to 650◦C, and then maintained a low value above 650◦C

With the increase in temperature, the deformation mechanism transformed from anti-phase boundary shearing to stacking fault shearing, and then from deformation twinning to Orowan bypassing, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: When a partial dislocation is cut into the γ′ precipitation, high-energy APBs are generated due to the a/2<110> displacement of the superlattice.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: The transition temperature from APB shearing to the SF shearing mechanism decreases due to the combination of higher APB energy and lower SFE [20]. Therefore, SFs will appear as the temperature increases.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: when the test temperature is increased, a large number of deformation twins are generated in the alloy
Deformation twins were generated in the deformed alloy with high-density stacking faults and they can contribute to the high strength.

evidence.section: 3.2.2. Microstructure Analysis of the Deformed Samples
evidence.quote: the deformation mechanism mainly involves the dislocation bypassing the γ′ precipitation through the Orowan process , and the dislocations pile up around the γ′ precipitation at high temperatures
the γ′ precipitates can play a role in precipitation strengthening
The main strengthening mechanism of the alloy was the γ′ precipitation, which could effectively block dislocation movement.
Co, Cr, Mo, and W are enriched in the γ matrix and play the role of solid solution strengthening
the applied stress value is less than the critical stress required for dislocation cutting γ′ precipitates, and then the enhanced thermal activation causes the dislocation climbing mechanism
